prize_parts.citation: for advancing the economic analysis of political institutions, state capacity, and fiscal policy

statement.case_for: B021 remains my preferred configuration. Besley, Persson, and Tabellini provide a coherent and complementary attribution for a mature body of work that brought political incentives, institutions, state capacity, and fiscal choices into systematic economic analysis. Its influence extends from theory to empirical institutional research and to central questions of development and public finance.
statement.case_against: The principal reservation is breadth: constitutions, electoral rules, state capacity, and fiscal policy contain several related literatures, and a final citation must avoid implying that the three laureates alone account for all of modern political economy. The case is strongest when framed around the common analysis of political institutions and state capacity rather than every application listed in the ballot description.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B021 first and argues that the three candidates are central architects of a mature political-economy programme, while warning that its breadth makes a three-person attribution selective.
responses.response: I agree with both the strength of the core attribution and the warning. That is why I would narrow the citation to political institutions, state capacity, and fiscal policy; the narrower formulation preserves the intellectual connection among the three without claiming an award for the entire field.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B016 above B021, emphasizing its consequential quantitative account of misallocation while noting sensitivity of measured distortions to modeling and measurement choices.
responses.response: B016 is an exceptionally strong alternative, but its central empirical wedges have a more model-dependent welfare interpretation. B021 has a comparably broad impact with a more unified long-run contribution linking political incentives and institutional capacity to economic policy; this makes it the stronger preferred configuration, while B016 remains an important benchmark.

uncertainties: Whether the final citation can delimit the shared political-economy contribution sharply enough to distinguish it from adjacent institutional and public-finance literatures.
The proper relative weighting of the candidates' distinct contributions to theory, evidence, and state-capacity analysis.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile.
